item.title: Trump insists he's "not rushing to make any decisions on Iran"
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: President Trump told an Israeli TV network on Thursday that he is "not rushing" and could wait until 2027 to make a decision on his next move in the war with Iran. Despite Mr. Trump's remark, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News Israel and the U.S. are considering launching a new assault on Iran in the short term, with the Netanyahu administration concerned about how rapidly Iran is rebuilding its weapons production capacity.Iran on Thursday rejected Mr. Trump's accusation that it may be seeking to develop chemical or biological weapons, with the foreign ministry saying U.S. allegations "keep changing" and are following "the same fraudulent script" as the justification for the 2003 U.S. invasion of Iraq.
New Updates
1m ago
Saudi Arabia intercepts 2 Houthi missiles, coalition says
The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said Friday that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis.
Saudi Arabia backs Yemen's government in the impoverished nation's more than decade-long civil war against the Iran-backed rebel group.
The latest missiles launched by the Houthis targeted the Jazan region, on the southwest Saudi coast near the border with Yemen, but "air defense intercepted and destroyed" them, according to coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki.
The Houthis struck a tower in Riyadh's financial district earlier this week.

item.title: Russia missiles pummel Ukraine and hit NATO soil in Poland
item.description:
Poland's government said Russian missiles landed in the country overnight as Vladimir Putin's forces hammered Ukraine with what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called "one of the largest attacks" since the war began. The strikes on Ukraine killed at least eight people, according to Zelenskyy.
The prime minister of Poland, a NATO member, decried the Russian weapons landing in his country as "an intentional provocation" of the U.S.-led military alliance.
"We know that what landed on Polish soil came from Russia. Therefore — ⁠and this is not just my own assessment, but ‌also that of our foreign partners, including those within NATO — it does not look like an ‌accident," Prime Minister ⁠Donald Tusk said. "It ‌appears that we ⁠are dealing with an intentional ⁠provocation."
Members of the Polish military gather near the site where an object fell, in Rudnik and Sanem, Poland, November 20, 2026. Polish authorities said they investigate at least three objects found near the border with Ukraine on Friday.
Kacper Pempel/REUTERS
"Russia is trying to compensate for its military and diplomatic impotence with precisely this kind of terror," Zelenskyy wrote, adding that Putin's attempt to "redraw the world" with his Chinese and U.S. counterparts during their summit Thursday in China had been a "failure."
"Hard to regard it as a coincidence"
Russia fired more than 400 drones and 110 missiles at Ukraine overnight and early Friday, including cluster munitions, Zelenskyy said in a fiery social media post. Some of the Russian weapons hit the Austrian embassy and landed near the Netherlands embassy in Kyiv, prompting France to call for a meeting of the United Nations Security Council.

item.title: U.S. and Israel considering new assault on Iran, sources say
item.description:
Tel Aviv — Israel and the U.S. are considering launching a new assault on Iran in the short term, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's administration is concerned about how rapidly the Iranians are rebuilding their ballistic missile manufacturing capabilities and the pace at which Iran is working to shield its military and nuclear infrastructure from attack by moving it underground, the sources told CBS News.
President Trump also said this week that Iran may be seeking to develop chemical or biological weapons, though he provided no evidence to support the claim.
Months of indirect negotiations between the U.S. and Iran have failed to bring a ceasefire deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran has refused to even discuss its nuclear program unless the U.S. lifts its naval blockade and accepts six other key conditions.
Israel's military is prepared for a new round of fighting with Iran and is in peak defensive posture to respond to any first attack by Iran, the sources told CBS News.
The Netanyahu administration would prefer to launch a new joint operation with the U.S., but the sources told CBS News it remains unclear whether Mr. Trump wants to order new military action, and if so, what kind. The war was a key factor in the Republicans' defeat in the recent midterm elections and it remains deeply unpopular with Americans.
The U.S. has significant firepower in the region, including tens of thousands of forces and two aircraft carriers with their associated strike groups, amounting to dozens of warships and aircraft.
For both Mr. Trump and Netanyahu, who jointly launched the war with Iran almost nine months ago with a massive round of strikes on the Islamic Republic, the window for any new collaborative action may be closing.

item.title: Iran may be working on biological weapons, Trump says
item.description:
Follow updates on the war in the Middle East for Friday, Nov. 20, here. See earlier developments below.
What to know about the Iran war: President Trump told Fox News on Wednesday there are indications Iran may be working to develop biological or chemical weapons due to damage inflicted to its nuclear program, as tension in the nearly nine-month war appears to rise.Iran claimed Thursday that two more oil tankers had hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires on board. Iran's daily claims of vessels hitting mines have not been corroborated, but the United Arab Emirates' state oil company confirmed one crew member was missing Wednesday after one of its ships was struck by a projectile.Bahrain and Kuwait said Wednesday they had intercepted weapons launched by Iran after the U.S. carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
New Updates
3:51 AM
Houthis say Saudi planes struck civilian boat, killing 19
Houthi authorities accused Saudi forces on Friday of attacking a civilian boat and killing 19 people, after Yemen's dormant civil war reignited.
Conflict flared up in July after years of relative calm, pitting the internationally recognized government, backed by Saudi Arabia, against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels.
Houthi health ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi on Friday condemned the "horrific massacre committed by the Saudi enemy planes, which targeted a civilian boat carrying more than 25 displaced persons ... which resulted in the martyrdom of 19 civilians and left 4 others wounded."

item.title: Putin says Russia won't negotiate with Ukraine after bridge strike
item.description:
President Vladimir Putin said Thursday that Russia will not negotiate with Ukraine on a limited ceasefire, citing a Ukrainian strike this week on a major bridge connecting Russia and Ukraine's Russian-occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Putin made the remarks to reporters in Russian after meeting with President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China. He said he had discussed the possibility of a ceasefire in certain areas of Ukraine, but would not move forward with negotiations after Ukraine's strike on the Kerch Bridge, according to the Russian state news agencies.
The 12-mile bridge, which Putin ceremonially opened himself in 2018, is hugely symbolic as it links the Russian mainland with Crimea — territory that Russian forces occupied about four years earlier. The missile strike this week wasn't the first time Ukraine had targeted the piece of infrastructure, but it inflicted severe damage. Russia also struck two major bridges in Kyiv the same day.
File photo: A view of Kerch Bridge in Crimea in July 2023. Ukraine struck the bridge in mid-November 2026.
Stringer/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images
Putin played down the bridge's strategic importance on Thursday and said he had heard the calls "from all sides" for a naval ceasefire or a suspension of strikes on energy facilities, but he ruled out direct negotiations with Ukraine, citing the attack on the bridge.
"Honestly, I discussed the issue with my colleagues at the Security Council, and I asked them to think about it and go back to the issue, so that we could reach some agreements," Putin said, according to Russian state news agency TASS. "However, we will not make agreements after strikes on the Crimean Bridge. We will respond to these strikes."

item.title: Trump meeting with Putin and Xi in China appears to achieve little
item.description:
President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin sat down together in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday in a rare face-to-face encounter for the leaders of three of the world's most powerful countries, but there appeared to be little concrete to show for the meeting in terms of resolving any of the crises facing the world.
The leaders offered a joint statement after their roughly hour-and-a-half-long meeting. Mr. Trump immediately left for his return flight to the U.S. without speaking to journalists on the ground. On the flight home, the president said on social media he will hold a press conference at noon on Friday to discuss the trip.
The presidents discussed Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine, which Mr. Trump has wanted to bring to a negotiated end. But the only significant statement on the conflict came after the meeting from Putin, who ruled out any direct negotiations with Ukraine, citing a major strike earlier this week by Ukrainian forces on a key bridge in Russian-held Crimea.
Putin's senior aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters after the meeting that the atmosphere had been good, and the Kremlin quickly released what it called a joint statement from all three leaders characterizing the talks. The White House later provided the same statement.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, center, President Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 19, 2026.
Mandel NGAN/AFP/Getty
